title: Increased Pseudorandomness Threshold
summary: For randomized permutations with constant output-bit locality, it remains open whether negligible distance from four-wise independence at T rounds guarantees pseudorandomness after doubling the rounds.

formal_statement.body: Let $P$ be a randomized permutation $P:\{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}^n$ such that each output bit depends on only a constant number of input bits. The unresolved question is whether, if the $T$-fold composition $P^T$ is negligibly far from $4$-wise independence, then increasing the number of composition rounds to $2T$ makes the result pseudorandom; specifically, whether there exists a polynomial $p$ such that $P^{2T}$ is a pseudorandom permutation under these conditions.

scope.domain: Pseudorandomness thresholds for repeatedly composed randomized permutations with constant input dependence per output bit.
assumptions: The T-fold composition is negligibly far from 4-wise independence.
parameters: P: randomized permutation being repeatedly composed
n: input and output bit length
T: baseline number of composition rounds
p: polynomial introduced existentially in the conjectured conclusion
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether, under the stated premise, there exists a polynomial p such that the 2T-fold composition is a pseudorandom permutation.

citations.label: When Simple Permutations Mix Poorly: Limited Independence Does Not Imply Pseudorandomness

progress.summary: The source explicitly labels the claim Conjecture 4, “Increased Pseudorandomness Threshold,” and motivates it by limitations of its counterexample when four-wise independence is required in intermediate rounds.
citation_labels: Jesko Dujmovic et al., When Simple Permutations Mix Poorly: Limited Independence Does Not Imply Pseudorandomness
